chapter: Movies and the Los Angeles scene
title: Making Hellzapoppin with Slim Gaillard
summary: Slim and Slam made Hellzapoppin through the William Morris agency in L.A.; Stewart was paid about $750 and met Olsen and Johnson and Martha Raye.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: How did you -- how did you come about making the movie that you're in now with Slim Gaillard?

Well, Slim and I, as I mentioned before, when we left New York, the first place that we hit was Los Angeles. And we were -- while we were working a couple of the clubs out there, we were approached to make this film or two that we made, and it just happened through our agent and, you know.

Martin Block, no, he wasn't on the scene then. It was the William Morris agent. In fact, the William Morris agent bought Martin Block's contract, and they were handling Slim (Inaudible) and myself at that time. So the William Morris agency did quite a little, few things for us, nice things, of course, like a couple of movies we were in. So that's how that happened.
How -- were you all well paid for working in the movies?
Well, fairly, fairly good. Let's see.

That Hell's A'Poppin' that Slim and I made, if I remember, my salary was about $750.00 during those days, you know, just to do a little segment there. I didn't think that was too bad, you know. So that was about it.
How was it -- did you all meet many of the people in the cast of the movie you were working on, or did you just go in and do the scene?
Well, we managed to meet quite a few of the people in the movie, Olson and Johnson.
Mischa Auer, I think he was in there.
